conclusion: A typical HTT repeat length, the same as most people carry: no raised chance of Huntington disease from this gene.
An intermediate length: no Huntington disease is expected in you, but the repeat can lengthen when passed on, more often from a father, and may reach the disease range in a child.
A reduced-penetrance length: some people with it develop Huntington disease, usually later in life, and many never do. About 1 in 400 people in the general population carry a length of 36 or more.
A fully penetrant length: Huntington disease is expected to develop over a normal lifespan, earlier the longer the repeat.
The HTT repeat was not measured, so nothing can be said about it.
